question.text:
You are evaluating three fixed income securities based on their yield and duration: Security A: Yield = 6%, Duration = 5 years Security B: Yield = 5%, Duration = 7 years Security C: Yield = 4%, Duration = 4 years
Which security is expected to provide the highest total return if held to maturity?

answer.text: Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: If all three bonds return principal at maturity, the security with the highest coupon/yield delivers the highest total holding-period return. Security A at 6% beats B at 5% and C at 4%. The Trap: Candidates who overweight duration (B has the longest horizon for compounding) pick B; candidates who overweight safety pick C. Both forget that 'held to maturity' neutralises the interest-rate path and leaves yield as the dominant driver. Cross-Exam Context: Yield-to-maturity and hold-to-maturity return mechanics are tested in NISM-VII (Securities Operations), NISM-XV (Research Analyst), and NISM-XXI-B (PMS Managers). Distributor's Pro-Tip: Remind HNI clients that mark-to-market moves are noise if the debt PMS mandate is accrual and hold-to-maturity - what matters is portfolio YTM at entry, net of fees, and credit quality.
